components.name: Primary Button
components.description: Bruin blue fill with white text; flips to gold on hover. Used for the main action in a section or panel.
components.css: .ds-btn-filled { display: inline-flex; align-items: center; justify-content: center; min-height: 2.75rem; padding: 0.75rem 1.25rem; border: 2px solid var(--button-selected-fill, #2774AE); border-radius: 0; background: var(--button-selected-fill, #2774AE); color: #FFFFFF; font: 800 0.875rem/1 "Plus Jakarta Sans", Arial, Helvetica, sans-serif; white-space: nowrap; cursor: pointer; transition: background-color 140ms ease, border-color 140ms ease, color 140ms ease, transform 120ms ease; } .ds-btn-filled:hover { border-color: var(--button-hover-fill, #FFD100); background: var(--button-hover-fill, #FFD100); color: var(--button-hover-text, #003B5C); } .ds-btn-filled:active { transform: scale(0.97); } .ds-btn-filled:focus-visible { outline: 3px solid #FFD100; outline-offset: 3px; }

components.name: Gold Button

narrative.overview:
The system behaves like a printed tournament program handed out at a UCLA math event: a blue cover, a bear mark, gold rules separating the sections, and a two-column body where the left column names the section and the right column carries the detail. It is editorial rather than app-like. Pages are composed from full-width bands, thin rules, schedule tables, and dense type — not from cards floating on a canvas.

The campus energy comes from scale and contrast: oversized display type on a saturated Bruin blue field, gold used like a printed marker, and numbers set tabular so times and countdowns line up. The structure stays institutional and calm, so the energy reads as confidence rather than noise. Warmth comes from direct copy, generous white space, and the bear — not from soft shapes or decoration.

The same grammar covers public pages, the tournament-day operations page, and the admin panel. Operate surfaces get denser tables and status blocks; public pages get more air and larger type. Both keep the sharp corners, the left-label column, and the gold marker.
keyCharacteristics: Sharp 90° corners on every control and container; zero decorative rounding.
UCLA blue fields and gold marker rules, with cool paper neutrals for reading.
Two-column section grammar: narrow left label, wide right content.
Flat surfaces; depth comes from tonal steps and 1–4px rules, never from card shadows.
Tabular numerals and schedule tables for anything time-based.
A deliberate dark mode that swaps paper for deep navy and keeps gold as the rule color.

rules.name: The Gold Marker Rule
rules.body: Gold is a marker, not a surface. Use it for rules, underlines, kickers, live status, and one decisive CTA. Keep it under roughly 10% of any screen; its rarity is what makes it read as UCLA.

rules.name: The Blue Field Rule
rules.body: Large areas of Bruin blue or near-black carry identity. Content sits on paper or night surfaces; blue is for bands, headers, footers, and actions, not for every panel.

rules.name: The Paper Default Rule
rules.body: Reading surfaces default to Paper or Surface White. If a section needs separation, use a tonal step or a rule before reaching for color.

rules.name: The One Family Rule
rules.body: Plus Jakarta Sans carries display, body, and labels. Do not introduce a serif or a second sans; the academic tone comes from scale, weight, and spacing.

rules.name: The Tight Display Rule
rules.body: Set display and headline leading at 1–1.1 and keep tracking at zero or slightly negative. Never add letter-spacing to lowercase display type.

rules.name: The Two-Column Rule
rules.body: On content pages, put the section label in the narrow left column and the substance in the wide right column. Do not center section headers or body copy.

rules.name: The 3% Gutter Rule
rules.body: Side breathing room is 3% of the viewport, not a fixed pixel value. The layout should feel printed and edge-aware, not boxed.

rules.name: The No Floating Card Rule
rules.body: Content never sits in a rounded, shadowed card. Group with rules, tonal bands, and spacing. If a surface needs to lift, it is probably a control, not a content container.

rules.name: The Square Corner Rule
rules.body: If a surface is rectangular, its radius is zero. Rounding a button, input, panel, or card breaks the printed-program metaphor.

dos: Do keep every rectangular surface at 0 radius and use 2px borders for controls.
Do use the two-column grammar: label left, substance right.
Do use Victory Gold as a marker on rules, kickers, active states, and one CTA.
Do set times, countdowns, and schedule numbers in tabular numerals.
Do collapse to one column at 900px and make buttons full width at 640px.
Do keep the global focus ring: 3px Victory Gold, 3px offset.
Do use tonal steps and rules for separation before adding any shadow.
donts: Don't round buttons, inputs, panels, popups, or cards; the system is square.
Don't add drop shadows or glassmorphism to content; the footer social chips are the only exception.
Don't introduce a second typeface, a serif, or a decorative display face.
Don't use gradients as decoration; grid textures and tonal bands are the only atmospheric devices.
Don't center body copy or section headers on content pages.
Don't let gold cover more than roughly a tenth of a screen; it loses its marker role.
Don't place body copy in Bruin blue on a blue field; use white or Sky Blue.
Don't invent statistics, testimonials, or future-event claims; the visual system must not imply proof the product does not have.
